title: Multiparametric Ultrasound Imaging with Contrast-enhanced Super-Resolution in focal LIVER lesions (MUSIC-SR-LIVER Study)
summary: Various imaging techniques are available for evaluating liver lesions, including, in particular, contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). This technique allows for a dynamic assessment of blood flow in liver lesions. As part of the study, in addition to the contrast-enhanced examination already planned for medical reasons, a novel, spatially and temporally high-resolution contrast-enhanced procedure (super-resolution CEUS) will be performed, and additional ultrasound-based measurements will be collected. These techniques enable a detailed visualization of the smallest vascular structures (microvascularization) as well as an assessment of the “properties” of liver masses and the surrounding liver tissue. The long-term goal is to improve the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound and thereby reduce the need for additional imaging procedures or potentially invasive biopsies.

interventions.name: The MUSIC-SR-LIVER study is designed as a prospective, single-center, clinical ultrasound-based diagnostic study. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Written informed consent
•    Known or newly detected focal liver lesion
•    Existing clinical indication for contrast-enhanced ultrasound
•    Sufficient image quality of the target lesion in the B-mode image as a basis for contrast-enhanced ultrasound
•    Histologically confirmed focal liver lesion, or alternative reference diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
•    Inability to give informed consent
•    Lack of a clinical indication for contrast-enhanced ultrasound, or lack of consent or capacity to understand the procedure.
•    Known contraindications to the administration of ultrasound contrast agents, particularly a history of severe hypersensitivity reactions
•    Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
•    Insufficient ultrasound visibility or technical limitations that prevent reliable SR-CEUS or elastography.
•    Lack of histological confirmation or lack of an accepted alternative reference standard
•    Withdrawal of consent
